stem: The Indian monsoon is indicated by seasonal displacement because of –

options.label: a
options.text: Differential temperature of land and sea

expl: The Indian monsoon is characterized by a seasonal shift (reversal of seasonal wind direction). Its direction remains from north-east to south-west for about six months (in winter), and for the remaining six months (in summer) it remains from south-west to north-east. The origin of these monsoon winds is linked to temperature differences, though there has been considerable debate on this. Two main concepts have been proposed for this— Thermal concept: The monsoon originates due to the differential heating/cooling of land and water and their opposite nature of warming and cooling; that is, the northward and southward movement of the Sun has a significant effect. Modern concept: According to the modern view, monsoon winds originate due to changes in air pressure and the shifting of pressure belts and wind belts. This concept was first presented by a scholar named Flohn.

stem: Amritsar and Shimla are almost on the same latitude, but their climate difference is due to-
expl: Amritsar (31º29'–32º03’N) and Shimla (30º45'–31º44' N) lie almost on the same latitude, but the difference in their climate is due to the difference in their altitude. Amritsar’s height above sea level is about 230 metres, whereas Shimla’s height above sea level is 300–6000 metres. In the manily troposphere, as altitude increases, temperature keeps decreasing.

stem:
declining of monsoon is indicated by:
(i) Clear sky
(ii) Pressure condition in the Bay of Bengal
(iii) Rising temperature on land
Select your answer using the following code –
expl: During October–November, due to the Sun’s apparent southward movement, the monsoon trough or the low-pressure system over the northern plains weakens and gradually high pressure replaces it. In the beginning of November, the low-pressure condition over north-west India shifts to the Bay of Bengal. In early October, monsoon winds withdraw from the northern plains. October–November is a transition period from the hot rainy season to winter. During the monsoon retreat season, the sky becomes clear and temperature starts rising, while nights become cool and pleasant. However, due to sufficient humidity, daytime weather becomes uncomfortable because of humidity-related heat, commonly called the heat of the Kartik month. In the latter half of October, temperature starts falling rapidly; this fall is seen especially in northern India.

stem: The powerful El niño in India is the cause of -
expl: El Niño occurs due to the accumulation of warm water in the eastern Pacific region near the equator. As the warm water heats the surface, moist air rises and storms form. As a result, the Indian South-West Monsoon generally becomes weak, and a tendency of reduced rainfall/drought is observed.

stem: India gets maximum rainfall mainly from –
expl: According to the data for the year 2024 presented by the India Meteorological Department, the major share of India’s total rainfall is received from the South-West Monsoon. In 2024, India received 935.9 mm of rainfall from the South-West Monsoon, which is 77.57% of the annual rainfall (1206.6 mm) in 2024.

expl: Rajasthan receives very little rainfall because the winds do not cross any major barrier, due to which they do not reach the height required for cooling. The Aravalli ranges, being aligned along the direction of the South-West Monsoon winds, do not act as an effective barrier in their path.
